source: Generated quiz 2026-10-24 14:53:03 (generated for bank) [orig: ITE 2015 Question 22]
question_title: Planning and Design of Software Solutions / Testing and Evaluation of Software Solutions (Question 22, ITE 2015)
prompt: While a program is running on the computer it unexpectedly quits with the error message “Stack overflow”. Identify the type of error and provide a brief explanation of the error type.

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies the error and provides an explanation of the error type.
Correctly identifies the error as a runtime error.

rubric:
A stack overflow error is a runtime error. These are errors which are detected by the computer when the program is running and are usually the result of a logic error in the program code.

The stack in this case refers to the call stack. For the call stack to overflow requires an enormous number of calls to subroutines to have been made. Generally this occurs as a result of an infinite loop containing a call or a recursive call that has no way of being resolved. As a consequence the stack gets larger than space allows and the runtime error “stack overflow” is raised by the system.

source: Generated quiz 2026-10-24 14:53:05 (generated for bank) [orig: ITE 2023 Question 22]
question_title: Provide an example of when a stub and driver may be used in software testing. (Question 22, ITE 2023)
prompt: Provide an example of when a stub and driver may be used in software testing.

criteria.criterion: Provides an example of when a stub AND driver may be used in software testing.
Provides an example of when a stub OR driver may be used in software testing.
Shows some understanding of stubs OR drivers.

rubric:
A stub may be used in software testing when you are using a top-down approach, writing top-level modules before lower-level modules. A stub would enable you to write placeholder code for the lower-level modules, allowing the top-level modules which rely on those lower modules to be tested before the lower-level modules are fully implemented. For example, if a game is being developed and part of the required functionality is to validate player names, the stub could be

BEGIN validatePlayerName(pName: String), returns Boolean

RETURN True

END validatePlayerName

This allows the rest of the program to be developed and tested, and the logic for this function to be added later.

A driver may be used in software testing when you wish to test modules of a program in isolation. This is commonly used for unit testing. A driver is written which functions as a test harness, allowing the module to be called and executed, and the result returned to the driver for comparison with the actual, known good result.

For example, if the validatePlayerName function has been written and needs to be tested, the line

PRINT validatePlayerName(“John”)

is an example of a very simple driver.

sample_answer:
The software debugger would be used to determine what is happening as the program code executes, to help the programmer better understand what the code is achieving. In turn, this will help them to understand either how the original code works, or why their modifications do not work as expected.

The use of breakpoints allows the programmer to specify particular points in the program where the execution will temporarily stop, allowing them to view the contents of specified variables at that point, or to change the contents (such as a flag that has been incorrectly set by the code) so that execution can continue normally to test if subsequent modules work as expected.

Single line stepping allows the code to execute one line at a time so that the programmer can see the effect of individual lines of code on any variables and output produced. This may make it possible to see the display of required information that may otherwise have been immediately overwritten by some other command, for example.

question_title: Comparing, Evaluating, and Replacing Algorithms for Matching Values in Sorted Arrays (Question 25, ITE 2015)
stimulus:
Consider the following two algorithms which perform the same function using two arrays. You can  assume that both arrays are indexed from 1 and that both arrays are sorted from smallest to largest.

![](assets/760da1a2-91de-4b3a-914b-feb852638944.png)
prompt: MysteryAlgorithmTwo is substantially more efficient with larger input arrays than MysteryAlgorithmOne. Contrast the logic of these algorithms, particularly in terms of  how the efficiency benefit in MysteryAlgorithmTwo has been achieved.

criteria.criterion: Provides a comprehensive comparison of both algorithms and correctly explains how the  second algorithm is more efficient.
Provides a description of the logic of both algorithms.
Identifies an aspect of the logic in one of the algorithms.

rubric:
MysteryAlgorithmOne contains an outer loop and an inner loop. The outer loop iterates over every item  in arrayOne (we will say that this loop executes M times). Every time the outer loop executes, the inner  loop iterates over every value in arrayTwo (we will say this loop executes N times). Therefore, the  code within the inner loop (which checks whether the item occurs in both arrays) executes M \* N  times. For an array with a large amount of data, this is a large number of comparisons and is very  inefficient. 

MysteryAlgorithmTwo takes a more efficient approach. It assumes that the arrays are sorted and  therefore can reduce the number of comparisons by iteratively reducing the lower bounds of the arrays  that need to be checked. This is done by eliminating the comparison of items when they are smaller  than the current item being evaluated. Only one loop is required, substantially improving efficiency.

sample_answer: Language-independent optimisation refers to techniques that can be applied across most programming languages. These include improving algorithm efficiency, reducing redundant code, and using better data structures. For example, replacing a slow sorting algorithm with a faster one improves performance regardless of the language used. Language-dependent optimisation involves using features specific to a particular language to enhance performance. In Python, this could include using list comprehensions, built-in functions like map() or sum(), or leveraging libraries like NumPy for faster numerical operations. By combining both approaches, a developer can write code that is both efficient in general and tailored to the strengths of the language being used.

question_title: Developing and Testing an Algorithm to Validate Australian Tax File Numbers (Q27, CSSA 2014)
stimulus:
The requirements for the validation of an Australian Tax File number (TFN) are as follows:

-   The number must be 9 digits long
    
-   A validity check procedure is applied wherein each digit of the TFN is multiplied against a given weight and the sum of these products must be a multiple of 11 (i.e. the remainder when the total is divided by 11 should equal 0).
    
-   The weights for each digit of the TFN are stored in the Weights array as follows:
    

Weights()

| Index | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weight | 1 | 4 | 3 | 7 | 5 | 8 | 6 | 9 | 10 |

-   The digits in each Tax File Number are also stored in an array TFN.
    

   eg.   A  TFN of 321 456 789 would be stored as follows

TFN()

| Index | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Digit | 3 | 2 | 1 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |

For example, a TFN of 321 456 789 would be validated like this:

Check length: Length of TFN = 9   Valid = True

Check sum:

3 x 1  = 3  
2 x 4  = 8  
1 x 3  = 3  
4 x 7  = 28  
5 x 5  = 25  
6 x 8  = 48  
7 x 6  = 42  
8 x 9  = 72  
9 x 10 = 90

The sum of 3+8+3+28+25+48+42+72+90 = 319

319 is a multiple of 11 (319/11 = 29, no remainder). Valid = True

Output:  TFN VALID True

Consider the following TFN\_Check algorithm, which is designed to carry out the TFN validity check for possible inputted TFN numbers.

The output of the algorithm should be either: TFN IS VALID  True   or    TFN IS VALID False

BEGIN TFN\_Check (TFN(), WEIGHTS())

TOTAL = 0

VALID = False

IF the length of TFN = 9 THEN

VALID = True

END IF

FOR n = 1 TO 9

TOTAL = TOTAL + TFN(n) \* WEIGHTS(n)

IF TOTAL = The reminder of TOTAL divided by 11 is not equal to 0 THEN

VALID = False

ELSE

VALID = True

ENDIF

NEXT

PRINT ‘TFN IS VALID?’, VALID

END TFN\_Check

-   Testing the case where the validity test will pass

rubric:
Sample answer:

The analogue signal, captured by a microphone, is measured at regular intervals (sampling rate) to create discrete data points. Each sampled data point's amplitude is approximated to the nearest value within a set range, determined by the bit depth, which defines the resolution and precision of the digital representation.

question_title: Explain how Opcodes and Operands create a link between programmers and the CPU (Question 29, ITE 2024 Y11)
prompt: Explain how Opcodes and Operands create a link between programmers and the CPU. Give an example of an assembly language statement in your answer identifying the Opcode and Operand.

criteria.criterion: Demonstrates an excellent understanding of Assembly Language and Mnemonics giving an example of Opcodes and Operands
Demonstrates a good understanding of Assembly Language and Mnemonics
Demonstrates a basic understanding of Assembly Language

rubric:
Sample answer:

Opcodes and Operands are a link between assembly programming language, a second-generation language, and machine code a first-generation programming language. Assembly languages sit between high level languages such as Python and C++ and Machine code. These languages are much easier for humans to understand. 

Assembly language uses Mnemonics Opcodes which are a shortened brief description of what is taking place – MOV for move or LDA for load accumulator, for example. Each mnemonic directly corresponds with a machine code instruction for the family of CPUs on which the code executes. As a result, assembly language is known as a one-to-one language. 

In x86 assembler the code MOV BL, 8 moves the value 8 into the BL register (the lower 8 bits of register BX). MOV is the Opcode. BL (register name) and 8 are the Operands.

The binary (machine code) equivalent of MOV BL,8 is 1011 0100 0000 1000. The first byte combines the opcode and the operand BL, the second byte is the operand 8 in binary.

prompt:
Describe how inheritance helps to improve the productivity of programmers.

Provide a specific example of inheritance to illustrate your answer.

criteria.criterion: Describes how inheritance can improve the productivity of programmers, including examples.
Describes how inheritance can improve the productivity of programmers.

rubric:
Inheritance helps improve the productivity of programmers in the following ways:

-   Reducing the amount of code to write (or rewrite). If a superclass can be written which contains generic behaviour then using inheritance the programmer can create subclasses which inherit that generic behaviour but can also extend and supplement that with their own behaviour specific to the subclass. For example, a superclass may be Car which defines all the generic aspects of a car (e.g. manufacturer, model, colour). Then, the developer could implement subclasses for different types of cars with specific behaviours. For example, FourWheelDrive which includes information about whether the vehicle as a diff lock. This saves the developer from having to rewrite and duplicate all the generic Car code in all classes which they write.  
      
    
-   Reduces scope for errors. More code generally results in more scope and opportunity for errors. Using inheritance the developer can reduce the amount of code they need to write (particularly, code duplication) as discussed in the previous point. This means there is less scope for error to occur since less code is being written.  
      
    
-   Reusability of classes. Using inheritance potentially allows classes to be reused in many different programs, and extended as needed. For example, the generic Car class could be used in many different programs, with each program subclassing Car to add their own custom implementation of subclasses.

Top-down design is an approach where the system is designed from the highest level of abstraction down to the more detailed and specific components. The process starts with the broadest overview of the system and progressively breaks it down into smaller more manageable parts, through a process called decomposition.

sample_answer:
Sequential files:

-   Data is stored and accessed in a linear sequence, one line after another.
    
-   New items are appended to the end of the file.
    
-   To access a specific item, the file must be read sequentially from the beginning until the desired item is found.
    
-   Simple file structure and easy to implement.
    

Relative files:

-   Records (items) can be accessed directly using a unique key, allowing for random access. This is possible because each record is of a predefined length.
    
-   New records can be appended to the end or existing records can be updated without affecting the positions of other records.
    
-   Suitable for applications that require direct access to specific records, such as database management systems or indexing systems.
    
-   More complex file structure compared to sequential files.
    

The key differences relate to the item/record access and updating methods along with the complexity of the files.

sample_answer:
The choice of paradigm for software development usually revolve around the requirements of the software, the skill-set of the developers and environment into which the program is likely to placed.

Imperative programming is a paradigm which describes computation in terms of statements that change a program state whereas declarative programming expresses what the program should accomplish without prescribing how to do it in terms of sequences of actions to be taken. An example of imperative programming style is Procedural programming in which the program is built from one or more procedures (functions or subroutines). Many low level languages use imperative style and many commonly used languages such as C++ use this style of program. Other types of programming paradigms such as OOP can also be considered a being Imperative programming types.

Declarative programming is a style of building the structure and elements of computer programs, that expresses the logic of a computation without describing its control flow. An example of declarative programming styles is logical programming languages. Logic programming deals with the relationship with data without specifying how this is actually achieved. An example of this language is Prolog and is used for building up relationships between facts and rules.

border(WA,NT), border(WA,SA), border(NT,Qld), border(NT,SA),

border(SA,Qld), border(SA,NSW), border(SA,Vic), border(Qld,NSW),

border(NSW,Act), border(NSW,Vic), border(Vic,Tas).
prompt:
The query australia(WA,NT,SA,Qld,NSW,Act,Vic,Tas). returns the following

as a solution:

WA = red,

NT = blue,

SA = green,

Qld = red,

NSW = blue,

Act = red,

Vic = red,

Tas = blue

If colour(green). is deleted the query returns False with no solution.

Discuss the processing performed by Prolog to evaluate the query in each

case.

criteria.criterion: Thorough discussion accurately describing the inference engine operation
Satisfactory discussion with good knowledge of inference processing
Limited discussion with some merit

sample_answer:
It is only possible to colour the map of Australia using 3 or more colours. Therefore when a colour fact is deleted, the query cannot be resolved and hence it fails with false returned.

Prolog evaluates each clause within the body of the query in turn. The first clause is border(WA,NT) - this expands using the border rule which first requires colour(WA) to be evaluated. If WA is red then colour(WA) is true. Next, colour(NT) is evaluated - if NT is red then this is also true. Moving to the clause WA \\= NT we find red \\= red which is false so Prolog now backtracks. We now try NT=blue as this is the next fact. Moving again to WA \\=NT ,we find red \\= blue so the rule border(WA, NT) evaluates to true when WA=red and NT=blue.

Control now moves to the second clause in the query, namely border(WA, SA). This time we have WA=red so we evaluate border(red, SA). The rule evaluates to True when SA=blue. Later in the processing we need to evaluate border(NT,SA) which will cause an issue if both NT and SA are blue. As a result the inference engine will need to backtrack and find an alternative colour for one of these states.

Evaluation and backtracking continues until all clauses in the query can be evaluated as true - the solution in the question being one such result. If colour(green) is removed (leaving just two colours, red and blue) then it will not be possible to find a solution. For instance in the description above we ended up with NT and SA being blue. If there is no third alternative then all possibilities will result in false and hence the entire query will fail with the result being false with no solution possible.

question_title: Understanding Assembler Execution and Register Functionality (Question 26, ITE 2020)
stimulus:
A computer architecture is implemented with the following assembler instructions.

![](assets/aaae9597-8ba4-4ca8-8a88-cb345cc5c8cb.png)

In this computer system, any value stored in memory address 0xFFFF will be printed to the console with the value being treated as an ASCII value.

The system has six general purpose registers (R0-R5) and also a constant register ONE which always stores the decimal value 1.

An assembler program has been loaded into a disassembler and a screen shot of the disassembler is shown below.

![](assets/0dd8856e-36f3-4f92-b8f0-0daedccb81f7.png)

Note

-   All numbers prefixed with 0x are in hexadecimal.
    
-   ASCII codes for the digits 0-9 begin at decimal value 48, and for capital letters A-Z begin at decimal value 65.
prompt:
What does this program do? 

In your response, explain the role of register R1 and describe the program output.

criteria.criterion: Response shows some understanding of the assembler code

rubric:
Prints all even numbers from 0 up to (but not including) the value stored in R2, which in this case is 10. Therefore 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 is printed.  
  
The value in R0 is used to track the number of times the loop in the assembler code has been executed - in other words, it is functioning as a loop counter. However, the value stored in R0 cannot be printed to the console as values printed to the console (i.e. stored in 0xFFFF) need to be an ASCII value. 

Therefore, R1 stores the ASCII code of whatever value is in R0. This is why when R0 is incremented at the end of the loop, R1 also needs to be incremented.

sample_answer: The logic paradigm requires the problem to be carefully described without the need to specify how it is to be solved. For this problem the logic paradigm works particularly well, as the facts and rules of the problem are relatively simple to specify whilst specifying an algorithm or the steps required to solve the problem is much more involved. For this reason the imperative paradigm would be a very difficult paradigm for solving this problem. Listing the specific steps required to solve the problem is very difficult. There is a whole plethora of decisions that are nested within other decisions that need to be considered. These decisions would be required to continually check if a neighbouring state has the same colour. Many such nested decisions result in an exponential increase in the number of possible outcomes that need to be dealt with. When using an imperative language all these decisions and how to deal with each outcome must be specified in code and then subsequently rigorously tested.. As we’ve seen none of these detail is required when using Prolog (logic paradigm) as the inference engine does all this heavy lifting for the programmer.

question_title: Role of the Program Counter During Subroutine Execution (Question 33, ITE 2023)
stimulus:
Consider the following algorithm.

1 BEGIN main

2 a = 1

3 b = 2

4 add(a,b,c)

5 print c

6 END main

7 BEGIN add(a,b,c)

8 c = a + b

9 END add

This algorithm is then coded in an appropriate language, compiled and run.
prompt: Describe how the program counter within the CPU is used throughout the execution of this program, with particular reference to the call to the subroutine and then returning to main.

criteria.criterion: Provides a comprehensive description of the use of the program counter in this program, showing an excellent understanding of the program counter and the stack
Provides a description of the use of the program counter in this program, with reference to the stack
Provides a response showing some understanding of the role of the program counter
Shows some understanding of the fetch execute cycle

sample_answer:
The program counter is a special register in the CPU which stores the memory address of the next instruction to be executed. When compiled, the high-level code above would be converted to a number of machine code instructions. A line such as c = a + b would actually be several lines of machine code.

When line 3 is being executed, the program counter would contain the address of the next instruction (line 4). Once the instruction in line 4 is fetched, the program counter is incremented to the next address in memory. However, line 4 requires the program to jump to the location in memory of the first machine code instruction in the subroutine add, this is accomplished by setting the program counter to this location. Note the current value in the program counter is first pushed onto the stack so that once execution of the subroutine add is finished, the value at the top of the stack is retrieved and placed back into the program counter. This means that the program can return to main at the correct position after executing the subroutine.

Note that memory locations associated with the parameters passed to the subroutine are also exchanged, however this is not directly related to the operation of the program counter.

The use cases for the data store, according to the DFD, are writing new records when a flight is booked, and reading them when the passenger checks in. For writing new records, it wouldn’t matter if the file was sequential or random access. For a sequential file, the new record could just be appended to the end of the file. For random access the data could also be written to the end.

However, for retrieving booking details, a random access file makes much more sense because if the booking reference can be used as a key then the record can be directly retrieved from the file, without the need to read any other records. sample_answer:
A typical assembly language instruction consists of an opcode and one or more operands. For example, an ADD instruction may have syntax… 

ADD Reg1, Reg2

where it adds the contents of Reg1 and Reg2 and puts the result in the accumulator. ADD is the opcode: the specific command which is part of the processor’s instruction set. Reg1 and Reg2 are the operands for this instruction: the additional data which specifies what the command should be applied to.

Another example of an instruction is:

JNE label

This is jumping to the location label when a comparison has been made and the values are not equal. In this case JNE is the opcode (the command) and label is the operand (the accompanying data).

source: Generated quiz 2026-10-24 14:52:50 (generated for bank) [orig: CSSA 2023 Q30]
question_title: The Interrelationships Between Hardware and Software (Q30, CSSA 2023)
prompt:
The Unicode Consortium was founded in 1991. Its method of representing characters in binary was extended to replace the existing ASCII code.

Explain why ASCII was no longer sufficient to serve this purpose and needed to be extended.

In your answer refer to the structure of ASCII and compare it with the structure of Unicode.

criteria.criterion: Explains the need for Unicode AND refers to the data structures of both ASCII and Unicode
Explains the need for Unicode OR describes the data structure of ASCII or Unicode

sample_answer:
ASCII was developed in the early days of computing as a standard way to represent American English. It only represented the letters of the alphabet and numbers as text. It also included various control codes for the hardware of the day. As such it only required 7 bits and represented 128 different characters.

With the global expansion of computing and communication, it became necessary to develop a worldwide system of coding which would have a single data item for every symbol used in the world. Unicode (utf8) uses 1 byte and incorporates the most used symbols. To preserve uniformity the first 128 characters of Unicode are identical to the ASCII set. Unicode also has larger datasets (2 byte, 3 byte etc.) and has plenty of room to include new symbols as they are created.

question_title: Controlling and Improving Streetlight Data Streams (Question 36 (f), ITE 2023)
stimulus:
A council is installing a new street lighting system. It consists of a light sensor and a set of streetlights. Every 5 minutes, the light sensor sends a data stream to a central computer. The computer broadcasts a single data stream to all streetlights to turn them all on once a day at dusk and then a second data stream is broadcast to turn them all off at dawn each morning.

Streetlights are turned on once a day and off once a day based on the following rules.

-   At dusk, when the light level falls below 20 lux, the lights are turned on.
    
-   At dawn, when the light level reaches 80 lux, the lights are turned off.
    

The light sensor to central computer data stream is structured as follows.

-   Header: 1 start bit (0)
    
-   Data block: 7 bits representing the light level in lux (a unit of light intensity), in the range 010\-12710. If the light level is above 127 lux it is reported as 127.
    
-   Trailer: 1 stop bit (0)
    
-   For example, if the light level is 64 lux, the data stream is 010000000.
    

The central computer to the streetlights data stream is structured as follows.

-   Header: 1 start bit (1)
    
-   Data block: 1 bit to turn the lights on or off: 0=off, 1=on.
    
-   Trailer: 1 stop bit (1)
prompt: Suggest how the lighting data streams could be improved.

criteria.criterion: Provides a reasonable suggestion on how the data streams could be improved
Provides a suggestion on how a data stream could be improved

rubric: Both data streams would benefit from error checking bits being added into the trailer. At the moment, an incorrect transmission could easily turn the lights on during the day or off during the night. For example, if an input data stream was corrupt at night, and the second and third bits were both received as 1, then the lights would turn off. Error checking bits would mean these types of errors are more likely to be detected. The system could then wait for the next data stream 5 minutes later.

- Preventing memory leaks – poor session handling, particularly in server-side storage, can lead to memory leaks, triggering more frequent garbage collection and degrading performance.

source: RESERVED – 2025 HSC (unseen until Sunday) — 2025 HSC Software Engineering Q21
question_title: 2025 HSC Question 21
stimulus:
Below is the _Issues_ table for a technical support company. FixTime, in minutes, is the time taken to complete each job.

| JobID | Issue | Response | FixTime | Category | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0001 | Cannot connect to the internet | Clear cache | 22 | Software | Pending |
| 0002 | Installation failure | Reinstall the printer drivers | 76 | Hardware | Pending |
| 0004 | Forgot password | Reset password | 97 | Software | Resolved |
| 0005 | Installation failure | Follow the installation guide | 110 | Hardware | Escalated |
| 0009 | Blue screen error | Run a system diagnostic test | 120 | Software | Pending |
| 0011 | Installation failure | Verify email settings | 45 | Software | Escalated |
prompt:
Construct a SQL query that displays:

- the number of pending software jobs
- the number of pending hardware jobs
- the number of escalated software jobs
- the number of escalated hardware jobs

List the results in order from the highest to lowest, based on the number of jobs.
dataset_setup_sql: CREATE TABLE Issues (JobID TEXT, Issue TEXT, Response TEXT, FixTime INT, Category TEXT, Status TEXT); INSERT INTO Issues VALUES ('0001', 'Cannot connect to the internet', 'Clear cache', 22, 'Software', 'Pending'); INSERT INTO Issues VALUES ('0002', 'Installation failure', 'Reinstall the printer drivers', 76, 'Hardware', 'Pending'); INSERT INTO Issues VALUES ('0004', 'Forgot password', 'Reset password', 97, 'Software', 'Resolved'); INSERT INTO Issues VALUES ('0005', 'Installation failure', 'Follow the installation guide', 110, 'Hardware', 'Escalated'); INSERT INTO Issues VALUES ('0009', 'Blue screen error', 'Run a system diagnostic test', 120, 'Software', 'Pending'); INSERT INTO Issues VALUES ('0011', 'Installation failure', 'Verify email settings', 45, 'Software', 'Escalated');

criteria.criterion: Provides a correct SQL query that extracts 'Pending' and 'Escalated' jobs for the 'Software' and 'Hardware' categories, counts the jobs for each status in each category, and outputs results in descending order
Provides an SQL query that addresses most of the requirements of the problem
Provides an SQL query that shows some understanding of the problem
Shows some understanding of SQL or the problem

sample_answer:
```sql
SELECT Category, Status, COUNT(JobID) AS Jobs
FROM Issues
WHERE (Status = 'Pending' OR Status = 'Escalated')
GROUP BY Status, Category
ORDER BY Jobs DESC
```

question_title: 2025 HSC Question 25
stimulus:
An airline introduces a virtual personal assistant as an initial support contact point for cancelled flights, missed connections, or lost luggage. The virtual personal assistant uses a neural network to:

-   analyse support queries to direct customers to the appropriate department
-   recommend appropriate tone and wording to be used by the human customer support representative
-   assess data such as support turnaround time, customer ratings, and repeat contacts.
prompt: Explain how the neural network supports the virtual personal assistant. Include ONE positive and ONE negative impact of using the virtual personal assistant.

criteria.criterion: Explains how the neural network supports the virtual personal assistant; includes one positive AND one negative impact of using the virtual personal assistant
Explains how the neural network supports the virtual personal assistant OR outlines how the neural network supports the assistant and includes one positive AND one negative impact
Outlines features of neural network AND/OR impacts of using the virtual personal assistant
Outlines a feature of neural network OR an impact of using the virtual personal assistant OR identifies features of neural network AND/OR impacts
Provides some relevant information

sample_answer:
Neural networks recognise natural language patterns to categorise common support queries, such as lost luggage, and use nodes to assist with processing. They assess language tone to gauge frustration or urgency, allowing the virtual personal assistant to recommend specific phrasing for customer service staff. For instance, calming language may be suggested for distressed customers. By tracking customer ratings and turnaround times, the neural network uses weightings to refine recommendations to prioritise high-frequency queries or improve suggestions for poorly rated interactions. While this system streamlines support processes and improves response accuracy, it may also impact the role of customer service staff. As the neural network learns from interactions, staff may rely more on its recommendations, potentially reducing their familiarity with emerging query trends or response strategies. Customers may come to expect faster, more precise service, raising the standard for human interactions.

question_title: 2025 HSC Question 24
stimulus:
A construction company introduces a safety monitoring system that uses artificial intelligence. Cameras and wearable sensors track worker movements and environmental conditions. The system detects unsafe behaviours through artificial intelligence, such as:

-   standing too close to operating machinery
-   entering restricted zones
-   failure to wear personal protective equipment (PPE).

criteria.criterion: Provides a comprehensive discussion of the impact of the safety monitoring system on workers with reference to the scenario
Outlines both positive and negative ways, that the safety monitoring system can affect workers

sample_answer:
The AI monitoring system can improve safety on site by reducing human error through real-time alerts and remote monitoring. However, some workers might feel their privacy is invaded, especially if the wearables continue monitoring during breaks or in private areas like bathrooms. source: RESERVED – 2025 HSC (unseen until Sunday) — 2025 HSC Software Engineering Q27
question_title: 2025 HSC Question 27
stimulus: Watch the video, and then answer the question. (The video is not available online: "Due to copyright restrictions, this material cannot be displayed until permission has been obtained.")
prompt: Explain how human bias could affect the usefulness of artificial intelligence (AI) solutions. Support your answer with reference to the video.

criteria.criterion: Explains how human bias could affect the usefulness of AI solutions; supports answer with reference to the video
Describes how human bias could affect the usefulness of AI solutions; refers to a scenario(s) in the video
Outlines how human bias could affect AI solutions; refers to the video
Identifies some sources/examples of human bias AND/OR identifies effects of human bias on AI solutions AND/OR outlines how AI learns
Provides some relevant information

sample_answer:
AI develops its ability by analysing vast amounts of data. The quality of these data can be influenced by human bias, and in turn, affect the usefulness of AI solutions.

Human bias may be explicit or implicit. Explicit biases are intentional. For example, a researcher may favour male physicists and only collect pictures of male physicists for training an AI solution, as shown in the video. Implicit biases operate unconsciously and may be shaped by social and cultural factors. Whether the bias was explicit or implicit, the choice of male physicists would suggest to the AI solution that physicists are male.

Human bias can occur in various stages of the development of AI solutions. As shown in the photo library example, training data needs to be diverse and representative, otherwise AI solutions may produce inaccurate or unhelpful responses. The process of labelling training data may also introduce biases as people may have different interpretations of the same data. The video shows that if most people draw shoes in particular ways, certain types of shoes will not be recognised as a shoe.

source: RESERVED – 2025 HSC (unseen until Sunday) — 2025 HSC Software Engineering Q17
question_title: 2025 HSC Question 17
stimulus:
An algorithm is required by a school to rate the risk of a location for school excursions.

A teacher completes a 10-question survey to assess potential hazards for the location. Each question is given a score from 1 (low) to 5 (high), and the scores are stored in a 10-element integer array called _Risks_.

The scores for each question are added to give a total risk score.

The excursion risk is rated as:

-   Low (total less than 20)
-   Medium (total between 20 – 35)
-   High (total above 35).
prompt: Using pseudocode, with a repeat-until loop, write an algorithm to determine the excursion risk rating for a location. You can assume that the scores for the 10 questions are already stored in the array _Risks_.

criteria.criterion: Provides a substantially correct pseudocode algorithm
Provides a pseudocode algorithm that addresses some aspects of the problem
Shows some understanding of the problem or pseudocode

sample_answer:
```
BEGIN RiskRating
    Total = 0
    index = 0
    REPEAT
        Total = Total + Risks[index]
        index = index + 1
    UNTIL index = 10
    IF Total > 35 THEN
        Rating = "High"
    ELSE
        IF Total < 20 THEN
            Rating = "Low"
        ELSE
            Rating = "Medium"
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
    Display Rating
END RiskRating
```

(The guidelines also accept a CASEWHERE or ELSEIF version of the selection.)

Knowledge of Python programming and the ability to apply logical conditions, loops, and string manipulation to assess password strength.

Ability to implement basic security criteria for password validation, including checks for length, uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and special characters.
sample_answer:
**Sample Solution 1**

import re

def check\_password\_strength(password):

    if len(password) < 8:

        return "Weak: Password should be at least 8 characters long."

    if not re.search(r"\[A-Z\]", password):

        return "Weak: Password should include at least one uppercase letter."

    if not re.search(r"\[a-z\]", password):

        return "Weak: Password should include at least one lowercase letter."

    if not re.search(r"\[0-9\]", password):

        return "Weak: Password should include at least one number."

    if not re.search(r"\[!@#$%^&\*(),.?\\":{}|<>\]", password):

        return "Weak: Password should include at least one special character."

    return "Strong password!"

password = input("Enter a password to check its strength: ")

print(check\_password\_strength(password))

**Sample Solution 2 ( without re module)**

\# Function to check the strength of the password

def check\_password\_strength(password):

    """

    This function checks the strength of a password based on specific criteria:

    \- At least 8 characters

    \- Contains uppercase and lowercase letters

    \- Contains at least one number

    \- Contains at least one special character

    """

    \# Define the set of allowed special characters

    special\_characters = "!@#$%^&\*(),.?\\":{}|<>"

    \# Check if the password has at least 8 characters

    if len(password) < 8:

        return "Weak"

    \# Check if the password contains at least one uppercase letter

    if not any(char.isupper() for char in password):

        return "Weak"

    \# Check if the password contains at least one lowercase letter

    if not any(char.islower() for char in password):

        return "Weak"

    \# Check if the password contains at least one number

    if not any(char.isdigit() for char in password):

        return "Weak"

    \# Check if the password contains at least one special character

    if not any(char in special\_characters for char in password):

        return "Weak"

    \# If all criteria are met, the password is strong

    return "Strong"

\# Main program to get user input and evaluate password strength

if \_\_name\_\_ == "\_\_main\_\_":

    \# Prompt the user to enter a password

    user\_password = input("Enter a password to check its strength: ")

    \# Call the function and store the result

    strength = check\_password\_strength(user\_password)

    \# Display the result to the user

    print(f"Your password is: {strength}")

criteria.criterion: Provides a comprehensive analysis of the environmental impact of AI and its applications.

sample_answer:
## **Environmental Impacts of Artificial Intelligence: An Analytical Perspective**

### **1\. Introduction**

Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are becoming increasingly integral to modern life, driving innovation across industries. However, their expanding computational demands raise significant environmental concerns. This analysis evaluates both the direct and indirect environmental impacts of AI and explores pathways to mitigate these effects through sustainable practices, improved measurement, and informed policymaking.

* * *

### **2\. Direct Environmental Impacts of AI Systems**

Direct impacts arise from the lifecycle of AI infrastructure—from hardware production to system operation and disposal.

#### **2.1 Production**

-   Manufacturing AI hardware involves mining and processing rare earth materials, resulting in **soil degradation, deforestation, and air and water pollution**.

-   High-tech chip fabrication is resource-intensive, with a significant **carbon and material footprint**.

#### **2.2 Transportation**

-   Although relatively minor, the transportation of hardware contributes **<5% of total GHG emissions** over an AI system’s lifecycle.

#### **2.3 Operational Energy Use**

-   AI workloads in data centers are a primary concern:

    -   Global data centers consumed **200–250 TWh in 2020**, approximately **1% of global electricity demand**.

    -   AI-specific workloads (e.g., model training) account for a growing portion of this usage, with companies like Google reporting **~15% of total energy use** on machine learning.

-   As AI models grow (e.g., large language models), **compute requirements have increased by several orders of magnitude** (e.g., FLOPS increased by 300,000x since 2012).

#### **2.4 Water Consumption**

-   AI operations also require substantial cooling, often involving water:

    -   Data centers account for **<1% of U.S. water use**, yet this can have **localised impacts** on ecosystems, especially in arid regions.

* * *

### **3\. Indirect Environmental Impacts of AI Applications**

AI’s environmental footprint extends beyond hardware, influencing various industries through its applications.

#### **3.1 Negative Indirect Impacts**

-   AI can amplify environmental degradation when applied to **resource-intensive industries**:

    -   Automation in **mining or manufacturing** may **increase energy and material consumption**.

    -   Algorithmic inefficiencies and redundant AI applications can **worsen overall environmental performance**.

#### **3.2 Positive Indirect Impacts**

AI holds transformative potential for sustainability:

-   **Energy**: Smart grids and demand-response systems.

-   **Transport**: Optimised logistics and traffic reduction.

-   **Agriculture**: Precision farming reduces pesticide and water use.

> Estimates suggest AI could reduce **GHG emissions by 2.6–5.3 gigatons** by 2030, supporting the **UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.

* * *

### **4\. The Growth of AI Compute and Sustainability Challenges**

The field has entered the **"Large-Scale Era"**, where training foundation models can consume **millions of kWh** per session. While **data center efficiency** has improved, these gains are outpaced by rising demand.

#### **Challenges Identified:**

-   **Hardware improvements** (e.g., chip efficiency) are **not scaling fast enough** to offset growing compute requirements.

-   **Lack of measurement standards** and **data transparency** impedes informed decision-making and accountability.

* * *

### **5\. Sustainable AI Practices**

#### **5.1 Technical Approaches**

-   **Model efficiency**: Use of pre-trained models, algorithmic optimisation.

-   **Hardware utilisation**: Choosing energy-efficient GPUs/TPUs and maximising utilisation rates.

#### **5.2 Infrastructure Strategies**

-   **Renewable energy adoption** in data centers.

-   **Geographical siting** of data centers in cooler climates or near renewable resources.

#### **5.3 Organisational Practices**

-   **Monitoring AI workloads**.

-   **Lifecycle assessment (LCA)** of AI projects before deployment.

* * *

### **6\. Policy Recommendations for Sustainable AI**

To support sustainable AI development, policymakers must:

#### **6.1 Establish Environmental Metrics**

-   Define **standardised indicators** for GHG emissions, water use, and biodiversity impacts related to AI systems.

#### **6.2 Expand Data Collection**

-   Collect AI environmental impact data at **national and firm levels** to enable global benchmarking.

#### **6.3 Improve Transparency and Equity**

-   Develop public **reporting standards**.

-   Promote **resource sharing** and **best practice dissemination**, particularly for **developing economies**.

* * *

### **7\. Conclusion**

AI is a double-edged sword for the environment. While it contributes to **sustainability goals through efficient applications**, its development and deployment processes carry substantial **ecological costs**. Balancing innovation with sustainability requires a coordinated effort among technologists, policymakers, and industry leaders to implement **standards, transparency, and sustainable engineering practices**.

source: Independent Trial (paper.is, via SEN Discord) Q23
question_title: New Question 23, Secure Communication
prompt:
Secure encrypted communication between browsers and web servers utilises the https protocol which includes SSL/TLS certificates.

Outline the exchange between browser and web server to:

-   Confirm the identity of the web server
-   Establish a secure session
-   Communicate securely during the session
sample_answer:
Establishing a secure HTTPS connection involves a crucial handshake between the browser and the web server, which confirms the server's identity and sets up an encrypted communication channel. This process is orchestrated by SSL/TLS certificates.

**Confirm the Identity of the Web Server**

-   **Browser Hello:** When you type a URL with https://, your browser sends a "Client Hello" message to the web server. This message includes the browser's supported SSL/TLS versions and cryptographic algorithms.
-   **Server Hello and Certificate:** The server responds with a "Server Hello," choosing the highest common SSL/TLS version and a cryptographic suite. Most importantly, it sends its SSL/TLS certificate back to the browser. This certificate is a digital file that contains the server's public key, the domain name, and is signed by a trusted Certificate Authority (CA).
-   **Authentication:** The browser verifies the server's identity by checking the certificate's authenticity. It confirms that the certificate is valid, hasn't expired, and that the domain name in the certificate matches the server it's trying to connect to. It also checks that the certificate was signed by a CA that the browser already trusts. This step prevents a fake server from impersonating the real one.

**Establish a Secure Session**

-   **Session Key Exchange:** Once the server's identity is confirmed, the browser generates a unique, single-use pre-master secret and encrypts it using the server's public key from the certificate.
-   **Decrypting the Secret:** The browser sends this encrypted secret to the server. Only the server, with its corresponding private key, can decrypt it.
-   **Symmetric Key Generation:** Both the browser and the server now have the pre-master secret. They each use this secret, along with other data from the handshake, to independently generate the same symmetric session key. Symmetric encryption is much faster and more efficient for ongoing communication than public-key encryption.

**Communicate Securely During the Session**
Once the symmetric session key is established, all subsequent communication between the browser and the server is encrypted using this key.

-   **Encryption:** The browser uses the session key to encrypt all data (e.g., login credentials, form data) before sending it to the server.
-   **Decryption:** The server uses the same session key to decrypt the data.
-   **Ongoing Security:** This process is reversed for data sent from the server back to the browser. The session key ensures that all data transmitted is unreadable to anyone who might be eavesdropping, providing confidentiality and integrity for the duration of the session.

source: Merewether Trial (paper.is, via SEN Discord) Q22
question_title: MHSTrial2025 - Question 22
prompt: Explain the three types of machine learning.

criteria.criterion: Students correctly explain the three types of machine learning
Students correctly explain two types of machine learning
Students correctly describe the three types of machine learning
Students correctly identify types of machine learning

sample_answer:
The three main types of machine learning are supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and deep learning.

Supervised learning occurs when an algorithm is trained on labelled data, where both the input and the correct output are provided. The system learns patterns by comparing its predictions with the known answers and adjusting to improve accuracy. This approach is commonly used in applications such as spam email detection, handwriting recognition, and medical diagnosis, where large sets of labelled examples are available.

Unsupervised learning works with unlabelled data, meaning the algorithm must identify hidden patterns or relationships without predefined answers. It is typically used for clustering, grouping, or anomaly detection. For example, businesses use unsupervised learning to segment customers into different market groups or streaming platforms use it to suggest similar movies based on viewing history. Unlike supervised learning, there is no “correct” output provided.

Deep learning is a specialised form of machine learning that uses artificial neural networks with many layers (“deep” networks) to process data. These networks can automatically learn features from raw inputs, making them highly effective for tasks involving complex, unstructured data such as images, speech, or video. For example, deep learning powers facial recognition systems, natural language processing (such as virtual assistants), and autonomous vehicles. Deep learning requires large datasets and significant computing power but achieves high accuracy in solving complex problems.

question_title: MHSTrial2025 - Question 29
prompt: Assess the impact of automation on the individual, society and the environment.

criteria.criterion: Students correctly assess the impact of automation on the individual, society and the environment
Students correctly assess the impact of automation on two of the three areas above
Students correctly outline the impact of automation on two of the areas above
Students correctly outline the impact of automation on one of the areas above

sample_answer:
The impact of automation can be assessed at the level of the individual, society, and the environment, with both benefits and drawbacks evident.

For the individual, automation often increases efficiency by removing repetitive tasks, freeing workers to focus on creative or analytical roles. For example, software engineers use automated testing to reduce manual errors and save time. However, automation can also cause job displacement, particularly in industries such as manufacturing or retail, where machines replace human labour. Individuals may require retraining or upskilling to remain employable, creating both opportunities and challenges.

At the level of society, automation contributes to economic growth by enabling mass production and lowering costs. It improves access to goods and services, such as self-service checkouts and automated banking systems, which increase convenience. Yet it can also widen social inequality if certain groups lose employment while others benefit from higher productivity. The shift towards automation may also raise ethical concerns, such as the reduction of human interaction in services like healthcare or customer support.

For the environment, automation can reduce waste and improve sustainability when systems are designed for efficiency. For instance, automated energy management in smart buildings lowers electricity consumption, while precision agriculture reduces fertiliser and water use. On the other hand, widespread automation can increase energy demand, particularly with large-scale data centres and robotics manufacturing, potentially contributing to carbon emissions if not powered by renewable sources.

source: Merewether Trial (paper.is, via SEN Discord) Q30
question_title: MHSTrial2025 - Question 30
prompt:
A program is required to compare the marks of two HSC students studying Software Engineering.

Synthesise a Python program that will:

-   Capture four assessment marks for each student out of 20, 20, 30 and 30 respectively (marks will be awarded for more complex data structures and error checking/validation)
-   Output the course total out of 100 for each student
-   Output the course average for each student
-   Identify and output which student has achieved the highest total mark from the completion of all four assessments

criteria.criterion: Students construct a substantially correct algorithm that includes:Correct use Python syntaxCaptures all required informationUses complex data structures [1D array or greater]Uses error checkingUses data validation or masking to capture correct valuesPrints all required information regarding totals, average and highest markUses sound intrinsic documentationInterprets without error
Students construct a correct algorithm with many of the features above
Students construct a correct algorithm with some of the features above
Students construct a correct algorithm with few of the features above
Students construct an algorithm that shows some understanding of the problem

sample_answer:
```
def capture_student_marks(student_name):
    max_marks = [20, 20, 30, 30]
    student_marks = []
    for index, max_mark in enumerate(max_marks):
        mark = input(f"Enter mark {index+1} for {student_name} (out of {max_mark}): ")
        while not mark.isdigit() or int(mark) < 0 or int(mark) > max_mark:
            mark = input(f"Invalid entry, enter a number between 0 and {max_mark}: ")
        student_marks.append(int(mark))
    return student_marks

student1_marks = capture_student_marks("Student 1")
student2_marks = capture_student_marks("Student 2")

student1_total = sum(student1_marks)
student2_total = sum(student2_marks)

student1_average = student1_total / len(student1_marks)
student2_average = student2_total / len(student2_marks)

print("\n-- Results --")
print(f"Student 1 - Total:", student1_total, "/100 Average:", student1_average)
print(f"Student 2 - Total:", student2_total, "/100 Average:", student2_average)

if student1_total > student2_total:
    print("Highest total achieved by: Student 1")
elif student2_total > student1_total:
    print("Highest total achieved by: Student 2")
else:
    print("Both students achieved the same total")
```

source: Merewether Trial (paper.is, via SEN Discord) Q32
question_title: MHSTrial2025 - Question 32
prompt: Describe web Content Management Systems (CMS) and justify why an experienced web developer would choose to use HTML, CSS and JavaScript while a beginner would use a CMS.

criteria.criterion: Students correctly describe CMS and justify use differences between experienced and beginner programmers based on the properties of the provided technologies
Students correctly describe CMS and justify use differences between experienced and beginner programmers
Students correctly describe CMS and identify differences between experienced and beginner programmers
Students correctly justify use differences between experienced and beginner programmers
Students describe experienced and beginner programmers

sample_answer:
A Content Management System (CMS) is software that enables users to create, manage, and publish digital content such as websites without needing to build everything from scratch. Popular examples include WordPress, Joomla, and Drupal. CMS platforms typically provide templates, drag-and-drop interfaces, and plugin systems to extend functionality.

For beginner programmers, CMS tools are valuable because they offer pre-designed templates, WYSIWYG (What You See Is What You Get) editors, and simple plugin installations. These features allow beginners to build functional websites quickly without requiring deep coding knowledge. The emphasis is on ease of use and reducing complexity.

For experienced programmers, CMS tools are used differently. They can customise themes through direct editing of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, develop custom plugins, and optimise databases for performance and scalability. Experienced developers leverage the flexibility of a CMS to integrate APIs, ensure security, and meet specific client requirements that go beyond the default tools.

The difference arises from the properties of CMS technologies: their user-friendly interfaces support beginners in creating basic sites, while their open, extensible architecture enables experts to create highly customised, secure, and scalable solutions. This justifies why CMS platforms meet the needs of both novice and advanced users but in very different ways.

source: Normanhurst Trial (paper.is, via SEN Discord) Q18
question_title: SE: SA - CIA (4)
prompt:
The school’s submission portal stores assessment files behind API endpoints such as
`/api/submissions/{classCode}/{studentId}/{filename}`.
While uploading, a student notices in the browser’s Network tab that the `studentId` in the URL is sequential. By changing this value, they can download other students’ files (the server does not re-check ownership). The portal also lets students re-upload a file with the same name via `PUT /api/submissions`, which silently overwrites the existing file. Finally, the portal accepts a client-supplied `submittedAt` timestamp that is not validated server-side, allowing students to backdate uploads after the deadline.

Describe how confidentiality, accountability and integrity has been compromised in this
scenario.

criteria.criterion: Clearly describes how confidentiality, accountability and integrity has been compromised.
Describes how confidentiality, accountability and integrity has been compromised.
Describes how TWO of confidentiality, accountability and integrity has been compromised.

Provides a response with some relevance to compromised confidentiality, accountability or
integrity.

sample_answer:
-   **Confidentiality:** Other students’ work is exposed through broken access control, changing `studentId` grants unauthorised read access to private files.

-   **Integrity:** The overwrite on PUT lets a student alter or replace a prior submission (even a graded one) and the unvalidated `submittedAt` allows backdating, so stored records no longer reliably reflect the true content or time.

-   **Accountability:** With no versioning or immutable audit trail, the system cannot prove who changed what and when; accepting client timestamps undermines non-repudiation.

-   **Synthesis/impact:** Together, these flaws break the CIA goals of the system, private work is leaked, records can be tampered with, and actions aren’t traceable, requiring server-side authorisation checks, server-generated timestamps, and write-once versioning to remediate.

ML models can analyse market trends, competitor pricing, and customer sensitivity to price changes. This enables Click Shoe Warehouse to set optimal prices that maximise profit margins while remaining competitive.

By using ML algorithms, the warehouse can segment customers based on their purchasing behaviour and demographics. This segmentation allows for targeted marketing campaigns that are more likely to resonate with specific customer groups.

ML can help identify unusual patterns in transaction data, enabling Click Shoe Warehouse to detect and prevent fraudulent activities, thereby protecting the business and its customers.

Automating the order fulfilment process can streamline operations, reduce human error, and speed up delivery times. BPA can manage order confirmations, invoicing, and shipping notifications efficiently.

Implementing chatbots and automated response systems can enhance customer service by providing instant responses to queries regarding product availability, order status, and return policies. This improves customer satisfaction and reduces the workload on customer service representatives.

BPA can automate communication with suppliers, track shipments, and manage procurement processes. This leads to a more efficient supply chain, ensuring that Click Shoe Warehouse maintains optimal stock levels and reduces lead times.

Automation tools can manage and execute marketing campaigns across multiple channels (email, social media, etc.). This ensures that marketing efforts are timely and consistent, while also allowing for data-driven adjustments based on performance metrics.

BPA can streamline data collection and reporting processes, providing real-time insights into sales performance, customer behaviour, and operational efficiency. This data can inform strategic decisions and help Click Shoe Warehouse adapt to market changes quickly.

By integrating Machine Learning and Business Process Automation, Click Shoe Warehouse can enhance operational efficiency, improve customer satisfaction, and drive revenue growth. ML provides valuable insights and predictive capabilities, while BPA streamlines processes and reduces manual workload, allowing the company to focus on strategic initiatives and customer engagement. Together, these technologies can help Click Shoe Warehouse achieve its business goals effectively.

question_title: Extended response: Communications (Q22, DoE, 2025)
stimulus:
An Australian toy manufacturing company has recently been established, with offices around the country.

Toy manufacturing is subject to strict environmental, workplace health and safety, national and international regulatory frameworks, enforced by the agency AusToy.
prompt: Compare and contrast Hybrid (also called WAgile) and Waterfall software development methodologies in developing software to control the manufacturing of their toys.

criteria.criterion:
The response clearly identifies and describes both WAgile and Waterfall methodologies, including key characteristics of each.
Effectively compares and contrasts the advantages and disadvantages of both methodologies, providing relevant insights for the context of toy manufacturing.
Demonstrates a strong understanding of how the methodologies apply to the specific context of toy manufacturing, offering a well-reasoned conclusion on which methodology may be more suitable based on the company's needs.

The response identifies and describes both WAgile and Waterfall methodologies, but may lack some detail.
Provides a comparison of the advantages and disadvantages, though some insights may be less relevant to the context.
Shows a moderate understanding of the application to toy manufacturing, with a conclusion that is somewhat reasoned but not fully developed.

guidance:
_Students may be awarded marks for any of the following:_

**Waterfall methodology**

**Description**: the waterfall methodology is a linear and sequential approach to software development. It consists of distinct phases: requirements gathering, design, implementation, testing, deployment, and maintenance. Each phase must be completed before moving on to the next.

**Advantages**:

-   **Clear structure**: the waterfall model provides a clear framework and timeline, making it easy to manage and track progress.
-   **Well-defined requirements**: since the requirements are gathered upfront, there is less ambiguity about what needs to be developed, which can be beneficial in regulated environments like toy manufacturing.
-   **Documentation**: each phase produces documentation, which can be useful for compliance and reference purposes, especially regarding regulatory requirements.

**Disadvantages**:

-   **Inflexibility**: once a phase is completed, making changes can be difficult and costly. This can be a significant drawback in a fast-paced manufacturing environment where requirements may evolve.
-   **Late testing**: testing occurs after development, which can lead to the discovery of major issues late in the process, potentially affecting production timelines.

**Wagile methodology**

**Description**:
wagile is a hybrid approach that combines elements of agile and waterfall methodologies. It focuses on flexibility and iterative development while still providing some structure. Wagile allows for incremental progress and regular feedback throughout the development process.

**Advantages**:

-   **Flexibility**: wagile allows for changes and adjustments to be made throughout the development process, accommodating new requirements or feedback from stakeholders.
-   **Frequent iterations**: the iterative nature allows for regular testing and feedback, which can lead to higher quality software that better meets the needs of the manufacturing process.
-   **Collaboration**: wagile promotes collaboration among stakeholders, helping to ensure that the software aligns with the evolving needs of the toy manufacturing operations and regulatory frameworks.

**Disadvantages**:

-   **Less predictable**: the flexibility of wagile can make it harder to predict timelines and budgets, which may pose challenges for project management.
-   **Potential for scope creep**: the ability to make changes throughout the process can lead to scope creep if not managed properly, potentially affecting the project's focus.

**Comparison**

-   **Structure vs. Flexibility**: waterfall is structured and sequential, making it straightforward but inflexible. In contrast, wagile provides flexibility and adaptability, which can be beneficial in a dynamic manufacturing environment.
-   **Testing timing**: waterfall conducts testing after development, while wagile incorporates testing throughout the process, allowing for quicker identification of issues.
-   **Stakeholder involvement**: wagile encourages ongoing stakeholder interaction and feedback, whereas waterfall may limit stakeholder involvement to the initial requirements phase.
sample_answer: In developing software for controlling toy manufacturing, the choice between WAgile and Waterfall methodologies depends on the company's specific needs. If the manufacturing process requires strict adherence to regulations and well-defined requirements, Waterfall may be more suitable. However, if the company values flexibility and the ability to adapt to changing needs, WAgile could provide a better framework for success by fostering collaboration and iterative improvements.

question_title: Question 11
prompt: Explain how the capabilities of end users influence the secure design features of software.

criteria.criterion: Explains causal relationships between capabilities of end users and the secure design features of software
Discusses capabilities of end users relevant for secure design features of software
Identifies a capability of end users relevant for secure design features of software

sample_answer:
Capabilities of end users, such as their technical proficiency, security awareness and accessibility requirements, significantly impact the design features of software. They influence the user interface, accessibility options, customisation preferences and security settings. Developers must consider the capabilities of end users to create secure, usable, and effective software. (Additionally, they should provide appropriate documentation, training, and support to users with different capabilities.)

1.  **Technical Proficiency:** End users have diverse levels of technical expertise, from beginners to advanced users. Software needs to be designed with intuitive interfaces and security settings (e.g. built-in prompts for secure actions) for less tech-savvy users, while providing advanced features for those who need them and can use them without introducing vulnerabilities.
2.  **Security Awareness:** Users' understanding of security threats and security practices differs greatly. Software needs to account for the varying levels of security awareness among its users and mitigate risks associated with less security-conscious users. Commonly, this includes providing secure defaults (e.g. requiring multi-factor authentication by default), restricting unnecessary user permissions and displaying clear security prompts. Software designers often need to balance security enhancements with user experience, ensuring that security measures are as seamless as possible to encourage compliance and reduce the likelihood of users bypassing security for convenience.
3.  **Accessibility requirements:** End users may have different accessibility requirements, influencing how security features are implemented. For instance, software design must ensure that security measures (e.g. multi-factor authentication) are accessible to users with disabilities, ensuring that security does not come at the cost of usability.

sample_answer: A template engine (a.k.a. templating engine) is used to rapidly and easily build web applications and dynamic HTML pages. It leverages HTML/JavaScript templates (some are pre-made but configurable, others can be written by designers) that contain placeholders, including variables, loops iterating over collections and conditionals. Different template engines (e.g. EJS, Pug, Handlebars, etc.) use different notations (syntaxes) to describe their templates and placeholders. When the web application is running, the template engine on the web server replaces the variables/placeholders in the used template file with actual values, then sends this dynamically customised HTML web page content to the client (which never sees the used templates). Templates also enable fast rendering of server-side data that needs to be passed to the application. By using a template engine, developers can separate HTML presentation structure from the application logic, making the code cleaner and easier to maintain. Designers can work on templates while developers focus on the backend logic.

question_title: Question 14
prompt: Compare and contrast cross-site scripting (XSS) and cross-site request forgery (CSRF).

criteria.criterion: Discusses at least 2 similarities AND at least 2 differences between XSS and CSRF

Discusses either ONLY similarities OR ONLY differences between XSS and CSRF
OR
Outlines a similarity AND a difference between XSS and CSRF
Provides some correct information about XSS or CSRF

sample_answer:
**Similarities between XSS and CSRF include:**

1.  Both XSS and CSRF are vulnerabilities that specifically target web applications.
2.  Both attacks rely on exploiting the trust that users and web applications have, particularly the inherent trust a website has in its users and their browsers.
3.  Both vulnerabilities can lead to client-side consequences, affecting what a user can see or do on a web application.
4.  Both XSS and CSRF can lead to serious consequences, including access to sensitive information, data breaches, account hijacking, and website defacement.

**Differences between XSS and CSRF include:**

1.  **Different focus:** While XSS primarily targets the user's browser and client-side security, CSRF primarily targets the server and authentication mechanisms.
2.  **Different attack mechanisms (vectors):** XSS involves injecting malicious scripts (typically JavaScript) into a website, which then executes in the user's browser when they visit the compromised page. Contrary, CSRF involves an attacker crafting a malicious link or form that, when clicked or submitted by the unsuspecting user, sends a request to the target website as if it were from the user themselves.
3.  **Different data handing:** In XSS the attacker can potentially read the response of the malicious script's execution and extract data to their own server. In CSRF, the attacker can only send requests, but they cannot directly receive the responses from the target website.
4.  **Different session requirement:** XSS can be successful regardless of the user's session status (authenticated or not), but CSRF requires the user to have an active session with the targeted website.

question_title: Question 16
stimulus:
An ISBN is the International Standard Book Number, a globally unique number to identify books. This is usually printed above the barcode on the back cover of most books.

The last (i.e. the 13th) digit in a 13-digit ISBN (International Standard Book Number) is known as the "check digit". The check digit is calculated in the following way:

-   Each of the other 12 digits of the ISBN from left to right is multiplied alternately by 1 or 3. This means that the first digit is multiplied by 1, the second by 3, the third by 1, the fourth by 3, etc.
-   The results are added together and then divided by 10.
-   The remainder of this division is subtracted from 10 to give the check digit.
-   If the check digit is 10 then it is replaced with 0 – this ensures that the check digit is always a single digit.

For example, in an ISBN of **9780980874921** the last digit (in this case 1) is the check digit. However, we should re-calculate that check digit to ensure that the ISBN has not been entered incorrectly.

(9×1) + (7×3) + (8×1) + (0×3) + (9×1) + (8×3) + (0×1) + (8×3) + (7×1) + (4×3) + (9×1) + (2×3) = 129.

Then, 129 ÷ 10 = 12 remainder 9. Therefore, the check digit is 10 - 9 = 1. In this case the ISBN is valid as our calculated value of 1 matches the provided check digit.
prompt:
In Python, write the function `checkDiqitOK(isbn_str)` that takes a 13-digit ISBN as the string `isbn_str` and returns True or False indicating whether the ISBN is valid in terms of its check digit. Assume that the provided string `isbn_str` always contains 13 digits – do NOT check whether there are fewer/more digits and do NOT check whether some of the characters are not digits. Do NOT write the main program nor any other subprogram calling `checkDiqitOK(isbn_str)`.

**Hints:**

-   The 13-digit ISBN is provided as a string, so conversion of individual characters into integer digits is needed for the calculations.
-   You can use Python’s `%` operator to calculate the remainder of a division.

criteria.criterion: Correct Python program that includes ALL of the following 5 features:Loops through each ISBN digit (except the last) and works out the sum of digitsCorrectly distinguishes between digits to multiply by 3 and add vs those to just addCorrectly calculates the check digitPerforms a check to see whether the check digit is 10 and replaces it with 0Compares the calculated check digit to the last digit of the entered ISBN and returns True if they match (correct check digit) or False if they do not (incorrect check digit)
Substantially correct Python program that includes at least 4 of the above features
A sound attempt at the Python program that includes at least 3 of the above features
An attempt at writing the Python program that includes at least 2 of the above features
An attempt at writing the Python program that includes at least 1 of the above features

sample_answer:
```
#Checks whether the check digit of an ISBN is valid
def checkDigitOK(isbn_str): #assumes a string with 13 digits provided
  sumOfDigits = 0 #accumulator for the sum of digits
  for i in range(12): #loops thru the first 12 digits but not the last/13th
    #1st digit has Python index 0 (even); 2nd digit has index 1 (odd), etc.
    if i % 2 == 0: #an even Python index, the digit is multiplied by 1
      sumOfDigits = sumOfDigits + int(isbn_str[i]) * 1
    else: #an odd Python index, the digit is multiplied by 3
      sumOfDigits = sumOfDigits + int(isbn_str[i]) * 3
  sumModulo = sumOfDigits % 10 #calculates the remainder of division by 10
  checkDigit = 10 - sumModulo #calculates the check digit
  if checkDigit == 10: #the special case; checkDigit must have only 1 digit
    checkDigit = 0
  #Checking whether the provided ISBN contains the correct check digit
  if int(isbn_str[-1]) == checkDigit: #last element is at Python index -1
    return True
  else:
    return False
```

_An alternative sample answer:_

```
#Checks whether the check digit of an ISBN is valid
def checkDigitOK(isbn_str): #assumes a string with 13 digits provided
  sumOfDigits = 0 #accumulator for the sum of digits
  #the first 12 digits of ISBN contain 6 groups of 2 digits:
  # the 1st of these 2 digits is multiplied by 1
  # the 2nd of these 2 digits is multiplied by 3
  for i in range(6):
    sumOfDigits = sumOfDigits + int(isbn_str[2*i]) * 1
    sumOfDigits = sumOfDigits + int(isbn_str[2*i+1]) * 3
  sumModulo = sumOfDigits % 10 #calculates the remainder of division by 10
  checkDigit = 10 - sumModulo #calculates the check digit
  if checkDigit == 10: #the special case; checkDigit must have only 1 digit
    checkDigit = 0
  #Checking whether the provided ISBN contains the correct check digit
  if int(isbn_str[12]) == checkDigit: #last/13th digit is at Python index 12
    return True
  else:
    return False
```
