question_title: Question 17
stimulus: Your team is developing the secure PWA ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA’. Using this app, a user first uploads images of their skin moles, personal information (e.g. name, phone number, email, …), demographic information (e.g. age, gender, occupation, …) and medical history. Then, the app uses machine learning / artificial intelligence to determine and show on the screen the probability of melanoma (dangerous skin cancer) in the given skin mole images.
prompt: Discuss how the 3 main principles of the ‘privacy by design’ approach should be applied in the development of the ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA’ app.

criteria.criterion: Discusses applying on the given scenario of 3 of the main principles of 'privacy by design'

Discusses applying on the given scenario of 1 or 2 of the main principles of ‘privacy by design'
OR
Outlines 2 or 3 of the main principles of ‘privacy by design'

Shows some understanding of 'privacy by design'
OR
Outlines 1 of the main principles of 'privacy by design'

sample_answer:
The 'privacy by design' is built around the 7 main principles: Proactive not reactive; Privacy as a default setting; Privacy embedded into design; Full functionality; End-to-end security; Visibility and transparency; and Respect for user privacy. From these 7, our Software Engineering syllabus emphasises only #1, #3 and #7 so their application on the given ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA' app scenario is discussed here.

**Proactive not reactive approach** is about anticipating risks and preventing privacy-invasive events before they occur. In the ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA' app scenario, the personal and medical information (possibly also some of the demographic information) is personally identifiable information (PII) that must be kept private and protected. It can be anticipated that this sensitive information could be compromised on the client side, transport over the Internet or the server side. Therefore, all information provided by a user should be protected (e.g. encrypted) in transport over the Internet and any client-side and server-side handling, including storage. This is protection in transit, in use and rest.

**Embed privacy into design** is about ensuring that privacy becomes one of the core functions of any system or service. In the ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA' app scenario, this means the app's design must include the decisions to protect all user's information in transport/storage/handling, not storing any user information (neither on the server nor on the client) after a user is shown the probability of melanoma in the given images, and not providing any user information to any 3rd party.

**Respect for user privacy** is about keeping the interest of individuals paramount for any system or service, e.g. by offering strong privacy defaults and user-friendly options, as well as ensuring appropriate notices are given. In the ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA' app scenario, the default protection of all user information in transit/rest/use, the default server-side and client-side secure deletion/destruction of all user information, and the default of not providing of any user information to any 3rd party are strong with respect to user privacy.

prompt: Explain, illustrate on examples from the ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA’ scenario and evaluate strategies that your software development team should use to manage security of programming code, including: code review, SAST, DAST, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing.

criteria.criterion: Explains and evaluates all 5 listed strategies for managing security of programming code AND supports this with examples from the given scenario

Explains and evaluates some of the 5 listed strategies for managing security of programming code (while only discussing the others OR explaining them but without evaluating them OR explaining & evaluating them but with errors) AND supports this with examples from the given scenario
Discusses all 5 listed strategies for managing security of programming code AND supports this discussion with examples from the given scenario

Discusses some of 5 listed strategies for managing security of programming code (while only outlining the others or discussing them but with errors) AND supports this discussion with examples from the given scenario
Correctly outlines all 5 listed strategies for managing security of programming code
Correctly outlines some of the 5 listed strategies for managing security of programming code
Shows some understanding of strategies for managing security of programming code
Provides some relevant information

sample_answer:
**Code review**, Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), vulnerability assessments, and penetration testing are all valuable strategies for managing the security of programming code, but they serve different purposes and are most effective when used in combination.

**Code review** is a manual (or partially automated) process of systematically examining source code to identify security flaws, logic errors, other mistakes or quality issues, and adherence to coding standards. In the ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA' app scenario, this would mean that some team members systematically review code written by other team members and provide improvement feedback. Code review encourages knowledge sharing, catches vulnerabilities and bugs early in the development cycle, reduces the cost of remediation, and enhances both code quality and security. Its limitations include: can be time-consuming and may not identify all runtime vulnerabilities.

**Static Application Security Testing (SAST)** is a white-box testing method that analyses source code for security vulnerabilities without executing the program. In the ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA' app scenario, some team members would use SAST tools to perform SAST on the app's code without executing it. SAST can identify vulnerabilities (such as SQL injection, buffer overflows, insecure APIs) early in the development process. Its limitations include producing false positives and not detecting runtime-specific vulnerabilities.

**Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST)** is a black-box testing method that runs software and analyses its behaviour (e.g. when exposed to simulated attacks) to find vulnerabilities that are only apparent during runtime. In the scenario, team members would use DAST tools to test the running app with simulated attacks. DAST identifies real-world runtime vulnerabilities and can find issues related to configuration and runtime environments. Its limitations include occurring later in the development cycle and being more time-consuming than SAST.

**Vulnerability assessment** is a systematic process of identifying, quantifying, classifying and prioritizing security vulnerabilities in an application. In the ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA' app scenario, team members would use appropriate tools to systematically scan for, identify and prioritise security vulnerabilities in the app. It provides a comprehensive overview of vulnerabilities and helps prioritise remediation efforts. Its limitations include not identifying all vulnerabilities and becoming outdated quickly if not performed regularly.

**Penetration testing** is performing simulated real-world attacks on a system to identify vulnerabilities that can be exploited. In the scenario, external hired white-hat hackers would perform simulated attacks on the running app. It provides a realistic real-world assessment of the security posture and identifies vulnerabilities that may not be detected by other methods. Its limitations include being time-consuming, resource-intensive and expensive, and it is a point-in-time assessment.

Incorporating a combination of these strategies provides a robust approach to managing code security. By integrating these methods into the software development lifecycle, the ‘nAIs Skin Check PWA' app team can significantly enhance their security posture and reduce the risk of vulnerabilities being exploited.

sample_answer:
The dataset exhibits a straightforward curvilinear relationship between the feature and target variables, characteristic of polynomial data. For such cases, polynomial regression is an ideal modelling approach because it can efficiently and directly fit the data to a polynomial equation, providing both accuracy and interpretability. In contrast, employing a neural network for this task would be excessive, as these models are designed to handle much more complex relationships that go beyond simple polynomial patterns.

Neural networks, by their nature, are complex and are optimised for learning patterns in complex data. When applied to this simple polynomial dataset, this increased complexity introduces a significant risk of overfitting. Rather than capturing the true underlying relationship, the neural network may instead learn to model random noise present in the data, which reduces the model’s ability to generalise to unseen data.

Training a neural network requires considerably more computational resources compared to simpler forms such as polynomial regression. Neural networks require iterative training cycles, which consume substantial memory and processing power, whereas polynomial regression can typically be solved with minimal computational effort. Therefore, for simple polynomial data, a Neural Network would be an unnecessary use of computational power compared to a less resource-intensive model, such as polynomial regression.

sample_answer:
The choice between using HTML and CSS versus a Content Management System (CMS) often hinges on the developer's experience level, project requirements, and desired control over the website's functionality and design. Here's an explanation of why an experienced web developer might prefer HTML and CSS, while a beginner might opt for a CMS:

Experienced developers are comfortable writing HTML and CSS code, allowing them complete control over the website's layout, design, and functionality. They can create custom designs that can be tailored specifically to the needs of the project without being constrained by the templates or limitations of a CMS. By coding from scratch, experienced developers can optimise website performance by minimising excess code, optimising images, and implementing best practices for loading speeds. This can lead to faster websites and better user experiences. When working directly with HTML and CSS, developers can implement any design or feature without being limited by the structure of a CMS. This flexibility allows for more innovative and unique designs. Experienced developers typically have a strong understanding of web standards, accessibility, and responsive design principles. They can ensure that their code adheres to these standards, resulting in more robust and usable websites. Using HTML and CSS means that the developer is not dependent on third-party plugins or systems, which can sometimes introduce security vulnerabilities, compatibility issues, or bloat to the website. For experienced developers, working with raw code can provide opportunities to learn advanced techniques, frameworks, and programming languages, further enhancing their skill set.

A Content Management System (CMS)typically has a user-friendly interface that allows beginners to create and manage content without needing to know how to code. This accessibility can be crucial for those who are just starting out. Beginners can quickly set up a website using a CMS, as many come with pre-built templates and themes. This allows for faster deployment without extensive technical knowledge. CMS platforms often come with built-in features such as SEO tools, social media integration, and analytics, which can be beneficial for beginners who may not know how to implement these features themselves. Popular CMS platforms have large communities, extensive documentation, and numerous tutorials available, making it easier for beginners to find help and resources. Beginners can concentrate on content creation and website management rather than on the technical aspects of web development. This can lead to a more immediate engagement with the website and its purpose. Many CMS solutions offer scalability, allowing beginners to start small and grow their website as needed. They also often handle updates and security patches, reducing the technical burden on the user.

In summary, experienced web developers may prefer using HTML and CSS for the control, flexibility, and performance optimisation it offers, allowing them to create unique and customised websites. In contrast, beginners often opt for a CMS due to its ease of use, quick setup, and built-in features, which enable them to focus on content creation and management without extensive technical knowledge. Each approach has its merits based on the developer's experience level and project needs.

question_title: Extended response: KNN algorithm (Q20, DoE, 2025)
prompt: Describe the K Nearest Neighbour (KNN) algorithm for regression, predicting y for a new data point using a training data set of x and y values given the K value parameter of 3.

sample_answer:
The K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) algorithm is a supervised learning technique that generates predictions based on labelled data. KNN is particularly effective for datasets characterized by a low coefficient of variation. The non-linear algorithm operates as follows:

1    Distance Calculation: For a given query (new data point), KNN computes the Euclidean distance (i.e., the straight-line distance) between the query and each point in the training dataset.

2.      Neighbour Selection: The algorithm identifies and sorts the training data points by their distance to the query, selecting the nearest K points (in this case, K=3).

3.      Prediction: The predicted value for the query point is determined by calculating the mean of the target values of these K nearest neighbours.

_Note: students can refer to any appropriate KNN distance measure, such as Euclidean, Manhattan, Minkowski, etc_

prompt: Describe the purpose of modularisation in software development and explain two advantages it provides for large-scale projects.

criteria.criterion: Clearly and accurately describes the purpose of modularisation using correct syllabus terminology (e.g. top-down design, system design phase, maintainability, reusability).Provides two well-explained advantages clearly related to large-scale software projects.Response is cohesive, detailed, and uses appropriate technical language.

sample_answer:
Modularisation is a software design strategy in which a complex system is decomposed into smaller, self-contained modules, each responsible for a specific function or process. This practice is essential in the system design phase of the software development cycle, as it enables programmers to apply top-down design principles and create programs that are easier to test, debug, and maintain. Each module can be developed and verified independently, then integrated to form the complete system.

For large-scale software projects, modularisation offers distinct benefits. It enhances maintainability, as faults can be isolated and corrected within a single module without affecting the overall system — improving reliability and reducing maintenance time. Additionally, it facilitates teamwork and reusability: separate development teams can work on different modules concurrently, promoting efficient project management, while well-defined modules can be reused in future systems, increasing productivity and software quality.

source: NSW Software Engineering Paper (paper.is, via SEN Discord) Q17
question_title: New Question 17, Encryption vs Hashing
stimulus:
The robot stores data internally, such as internal logs, and also communicates with other robots and users across the web securely via a wireless network which is password protected. All data for these tasks is secured using either encryption or hashing.

Additionally, hashed values are appended to the files that the robot transfers.

![image](assets/pp-nsw-software-engineering-paper-17.png.png)

![](assets/pp-nsw-software-engineering-paper-17.png.png)
prompt: Compare the purpose and function of the robot's use of encryption and hashing for storing and communicating data.

criteria.criterion: Provides the differences between hashing and encryption in terms of:Purpose, must mention the purpose of the hashes (tampering) etcHow they work (function), must mention keys, and properties of hashesProvides multiple references with the stimulus including for:Internal logsSecure wireless communication. Mentions TLS/SSL protocols.-1 mark for each not met

sample_answer:
Encryption and hashing are both cryptographic methods used to secure data, but they have different purposes:

Encryption ensures confidentiality (keeping data secret) by converting readable plaintext into unreadable ciphertext. There are two types of encryption:
Symmetric Encryption (e.g., AES): Used for bulk encryption of stored data (data at rest), such as internal sensitive logs, ensuring that if storage is accessed, the data is unreadable without the key.
Asymmetric Encryption (e.g., RSA): Used in securing communications (data in transit) with protocols such as SSL/TLS for the secure exchange of session keys, which then encrypt the data transmitted wirelessly.

Hashing ensures integrity (preventing/detecting unauthorized modification) and irreversibility with a hash function that produces a fixed-size, irreversible string (hash value) from the input.
Passwords for the wireless network access must be hashed before storage to prevent retrieval in plaintext, leveraging the irreversibility property. Hashing is used to generate checksums or digital signatures, which are vital for verifying that data packets sent across the wireless network have not been tampered with or altered during transmission.

question_title: New Question 21, Authorisation vs Authentication
prompt: Compare and contrast authorisation and authentication measures when designing a login portal for a fast food restaurant.

criteria.criterion: Compares and contrasts authorisation and authentication in the context of designing a fast food login portal.
Compares authorisation and authentication without reference to the stimulus ORExplains authorisation and authentication with no comparison
Outlines authorisation and authentication ORExplains one of them with sufficient detail
Provides some relevant information

sample_answer:
Authentication is the ability of a system to verify a user's identity, using passwords, MFA, or security questions, in order to protect systems from inappropriate access by bad actors. In this restaurant's login portal, usernames and passwords should be required to log into the website to order food or perform employee-related activities, and hashing algorithms should be used to secure the passwords of employees and customers.

Authorisation also relates to securing a system, however, it is the managing of permissions for such systems through this authentication, specific users or roles should be given different levels of access throughout a system as per the principle of least privilege. For instance, role based access control can be implemented by ensuring base level employees have the required levels of clearance to perform their jobs, higher than the customers, but managers who require more features, such as monitoring information not available to employees, can access it.

Hence, authorisation and authentication work together to keep a website secure, but the results of authentication will often dictate the authorisation provided to an individual.

question_title: Question 22 sql
stimulus:
You are a data analyst for an online retail company tasked with analyzing sales data to find the most consistently high-performing product categories. The goal is to identify categories that generate significant revenue through a high volume of sales.

You have access to the `Sales_Transactions` table:

**Table: Sales\_Transactions**

| Transaction\_ID | Product\_Name | Category | Unit\_Price | Quantity | Order\_Date | Region |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1001 | Wireless Mouse | Electronics | 75 | 2 | 2024-03-15 | North |
| 1002 | SQL for Pro | Books | 50 | 3 | 2024-04-22 | South |
| 1003 | Gaming Keyboard | Electronics | 150 | 1 | 2024-03-20 | North |
| 1004 | The Martian | Books | 25 | 2 | 2024-05-10 | North |
| 1005 | T-Shirt | Apparel | 30 | 5 | 2024-03-18 | West |
| 1006 | Smart Watch | Electronics | 450 | 1 | 2024-06-05 | North |

**Expected Output**

| Category | Number\_of\_Transactions | Total\_Items\_Sold | Average\_Items\_Per\_Transaction | Total\_Revenue | Highest\_Unit\_Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Books | 2 | 5 | 2.5 | 200 | 50 |
| Electronics | 1 | 2 | 2 | 150 | 75 |
| Apparel | 1 | 5 | 5 | 150 | 30 |
prompt:
Write a single SQL query to identify the top-performing product categories from all sales in 2024.

Your query must:

-   Only include transactions where the **Quantity** of items sold was greater than 1.
-   For each category, calculate and display:
    -   The category name.
    -   Total number of transactions.
    -   Total number of items sold.
    -   Average items sold per transaction.
    -   Total revenue, as the sum of.
    -   The highest price of a single unit sold.
-   Sort the final results by **Total\_Revenue** in descending order.
dataset_setup_sql:
CREATE TABLE Sales_Transactions (
    Transaction_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Product_Name TEXT,
    Category TEXT,
    Unit_Price REAL,
    Quantity INTEGER,
    Order_Date TEXT,
    Region TEXT
);

INSERT INTO Sales_Transactions (Transaction_ID, Product_Name, Category, Unit_Price, Quantity, Order_Date, Region) VALUES
(1001, 'Wireless Mouse', 'Electronics', 75, 2, '2024-03-15', 'North'),
(1002, 'SQL for Pro', 'Books', 50, 3, '2024-04-22', 'South'),
(1003, 'Gaming Keyboard', 'Electronics', 150, 1, '2024-03-20', 'North'),
(1004, 'The Martian', 'Books', 25, 2, '2024-05-10', 'North'),
(1005, 'T-Shirt', 'Apparel', 30, 5, '2024-03-18', 'West'),
(1006, 'Smart Watch', 'Electronics', 450, 1, '2024-06-05', 'North');

criteria.criterion: Correct Calculations: The SELECT clause includes all five required calculationsCorrect Aliases: All five calculated columns are correctly renamed using AS to match the names in the "Expected Output" tableCorrect Filtering: The WHERE clause correctly filters the data for both required conditions using AND: Quantity > 1 and accurately selects for the year 2024Correct Grouping: The query correctly groups the aggregated results by Category using the GROUP BY Category clause.Correct Sorting: The final result set is correctly sorted by Total_Revenue in descending order using the ORDER BY Total_Revenue DESC clause.-1 mark for each not met

sample_answer:
```
SELECT
    Category,
    COUNT(Transaction_ID) AS Number_of_Transactions,
    SUM(Quantity) AS Total_Items_Sold,
    AVG(Quantity) AS Average_Items_Per_Transaction,
    SUM(Unit_Price * Quantity) AS Total_Revenue,
    MAX(Unit_Price) AS Highest_Unit_Price
FROM
    Sales_Transactions
WHERE
    Quantity > 1
    AND Order_Date >= '2024-01-01'
    AND Order_Date <= '2024-12-31'
GROUP BY
    Category
ORDER BY
    Total_Revenue DESC;
```

question_title: New Question 23, RL Model Failure Analysis
stimulus:
A mystery mark student (inventors) had an innovative idea to make a pricing strategy business model for a technology audience, and it was very successful and used by many consumers. However, one day the RL model decided to not do what it is supposed to do. Here is the slideshow of the incomplete investigation carried by the mystery mark student.

![image](assets/pp-nsw-software-engineering-paper-23-1.png.png)

![image](assets/pp-nsw-software-engineering-paper-23-2.png.png)

![image](assets/pp-nsw-software-engineering-paper-23-3.png.png)

![](assets/pp-nsw-software-engineering-paper-23-1.png.png)

![](assets/pp-nsw-software-engineering-paper-23-2.png.png)

![](assets/pp-nsw-software-engineering-paper-23-3.png.png)
prompt: Critically evaluate the failure of Security by Design (SbD) principles in this scenario and how these can be mitigated with appropriate exception and session management, and at TWO other techniques you have learnt in this course.

criteria.criterion: 2 - Explains failure of 2 SbD principles, description, cause and effect must be evident. Note: SbD includes CIA triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability), Authentication, Authorisation, and Accountability (AAA) and Defensive Coding. Explicit correct description must be provided for at least TWO of them (as it says ‘principles’)3- Exception and Session management: Clearly describes what is checked, the response, and how it mitigates the issue(s).3- Explains how the two tools chosen could have been used to mitigate the impacts.-marks for each not met

sample_answer:
**SbD Failure 1: Defensive Coding**
The system intentionally bypassed the Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) layer \[slide 1\]. The ORM is a critical security and abstraction layer, handling tasks like query parameterization, managing transaction scopes, and ensuring data consistency. Bypassing it removed a key defensive layer, leaving the database directly exposed to potentially flawed logic from the RL agent.

**SbD Failure 2: Accountability**
RL agent was granted excessive privileges, allowing it to execute raw SQL UPDATE commands directly against the database. This violates the principle of least privilege, which dictates that a component should only have the bare minimum permissions necessary to perform its function. The agent was over-authorized, giving it the power to cause widespread damage.

**Exception Management:**
To prevent a complete system crash, exception management must check for database errors indicating that a physical resource limit has been reached and when such an exception is caught, the response should immediately trigger an alert to the team. The application could enter a safe mode, gracefully rejecting new pricing update requests from the RL agent. This prevents a disorderly crash by handling the error gracefully, which protects the integrity of all data committed before the resource limit was hit.

**Session Management:**
Database sessions should be managed to enforce transaction isolation levels. This ensures that concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other, preventing the race conditions described. The application should manage the lifecycle of a transaction within a controlled session, committing only upon successful completion of all required steps.

**Input sanitisation:**
As RL agent's output must be treated as untrusted user input, as a black box system, sanitisation is essential. Sanitising the input variables passed to the raw UPDATE command, or escaping special characters, would prevent the execution of malicious or conflicting code (such as potential SQL injection if the agent's logic were compromised)

**DAST tools:**
DAST could have provided a realistic assessment of the security strength of the live system. It would have been used to actively test the endpoints that the high-velocity RL agent was using and uncovered the weakness caused by the ORM bypass or exposed the race condition under high load, allowing these critical flaws to be fixed before the production crash.

**Answers may also include:**

**SbD Failure 1: Defensive Coding**
Could also mention
• The system treats the raw SQL generated by the black box RL agent as a trusted input. Defensive coding mandates that all inputs, especially from complex or external components, must be considered potentially hostile or malformed. By executing this SQL directly, the application created a potential vulnerability path.
• A defensively coded system should anticipate and handle errors (like resource limits or transaction conflicts) gracefully, rather than allowing them to cause a complete system failure.

**SbD Failure 3: Integrity**
The use of concurrent, unsynchronized modifications on shared database records led to an unpredictable race condition, resulting in compromised data integrity \[Slide 3\]. Integrity ensures that data remains accurate, consistent, and trustworthy throughout its lifecycle, preventing unauthorized modification. The core purpose was undermined when the outcomes of concurrent operations depended on the unpredictable order of execution of race conditions. Additionally the high-velocity data streams \[Slide 1\] introduces the challenge of handling massive datasets, which may be inputted.

**SbD Failure 4: Accountability**
Accountability requires maintaining logging and auditing mechanisms so that every action and security event can be traced back to a responsible individual or entity. As the "data corruption is untraceable and obstructs any form of accountability"\[slide 3\] because the model's logic is a black box. Without a clear audit trail, it is impossible to determine why the faulty commands were generated or to hold the system's designers responsible.

**SbD Failure 5: Availability**
Since the "database crashed with its storage resources exceeded." The uncontrolled updates caused transaction log bloating or data file growth beyond provisioned limits, resulting in a denial of service (DoS), and thus lack of availability or all consumers and the business itself.

**Exception Management**
The exception handler can check for database constraint violations that the uncontrolled RL may make, such as attempting to insert a negative price or updating a ProductID that doesn't exist. The response is to catch the specific exception, log it as a critical failure of the agent's logic, and trigger a Rollback. It should also generate an alert, preventing the database from being polluted with nonsensical or invalid data, preserving data quality and integrity by strictly enforcing the business rules.

**Implementing API**
Instead of allowing the RL agent to generate raw UPDATE commands, it should be restricted to calling a predefined stored procedure. This acts as a controlled API to the database. The stored procedure itself would contain the necessary logic for validation (e.g., ensuring the price is within a valid range), logging the change for accountability, and implementing concurrency controls like row-level locking to prevent race conditions. This abstracts the risky database operations away from the "black box" agent.

**Locks:**
The section of code that performs the price update must only have one thread that can access and modify that database record at a time. This ensures that when the RL agent decides on a new price for a shared record, only one at a time. This guarantees that the final state of the price (the outcome) is predictable and maintains data integrity.

**Audit Trails:**
The system must maintain detailed logs of user actions, access attempts, and security events. Specifically, every price update transaction initiated by the RL agent must be logged, including the input data used by the model, the resulting raw SQL, the timing of the transaction attempt, allowing traceability and ability investigate the logs and retrospectively determine the exact sequence of events that led to data corruption, ensuring accountability even if the model logic itself is opaque.

prompt:
The mystery mark student hired his band 6 classmate that he knew on NSW SENG. He quickly pentested and noticed that it is highly vulnerable to bot attacks and brute forcing, which could compromise their server and overwhelm their RL agent. Luckily no one had attempted this attack yet, but by SbD principles he suggested:

-   A time-based one-time password (TOTP) from an authenticator app.
-   A visual CAPTCHA to prevent bots.

However, the mystery mark student suggests that apps should be easy to use, especially for elderly or non-technical users.

Explain the ethical problem with implementing a purely visual CAPTCHA, specifically in the context of web accessibility, and propose the alternative secure solution.

criteria.criterion: Identifies the ethical problem (discrimination)Explains with an example of how it could be inaccessibleExplains a valid alternate secure solution-1 mark for each not met

sample_answer:
The primary ethical problem with a purely visual CAPTCHA is exclusion and discrimination based on ability. For instance, users who are blind or have low vision cannot perceive the distorted text or images, and users with dyslexia or other cognitive disabilities may struggle to interpret the characters. Rate Limiting addresses brute-force attempts by restricting the number of API requests allowed within a specific time window, preventing the server from being overwhelmed.

**Answers could include:**

A behaviour-based system like Google's reCAPTCHA v3 can work invisibly in the background, by monitoring user behaviour on the site to generate a risk score and present further tests only if the score is high.

question_title: 15 - PF - Require/Specs (BHHS, Prelim Yearly, 2025)
stimulus:
Explain the difference between requirements definition and determining specifications in the software development process.

In your answer, refer to the perspectives of both the client and the developer.

criteria.criterion: Explains BOTH Requirements Definition and Determining Specifications, WITH BOTH perspectives referenced
Describes BOTH Requirements Definition and Determining Specifications, with a perspective referenced
Outlines BOTH Requirements Definition and Determining Specifications

sample_answer:
Requirements definition identifies the features and behaviours the client needs from the system, expressed in business terms. It focuses on what the system must achieve. For example, a requirement might be: The system must notify customers when their order is ready for pickup.

Determining specifications translates these requirements into precise technical details for developers. Specifications explain how the requirement will be met, through functional specifications (inputs, processes, outputs) and non-functional specifications (performance, usability, security). For example: The system shall use an API to send an SMS to the customer’s registered number within 5 seconds of the order status changing to ready.

In short, requirements are written for the client’s understanding, while specifications are written for developers to implement.

question_title: 16v2 - Mecha - pseudo (BHHS, Prelim Yearly, 2025)
stimulus:
A robot vacuum cleaner utilises microswitches on it's bumpers to detect if it hits objects.

The following functions are prebuilt into the robot's codebase.

-   MoveForward(): Moves the vacuum one step forward.
-   TurnLeft(): Turns the vacuum 30 degrees to the left.
-   TurnRight(): Turns the vacuum 30 degrees to the right.
-   CheckObstacle(): Returns TRUE if there is an obstacle (wall or furniture) in front of the robot, otherwise FALSE.

The robot will need to follow the below key instructions:

-   The robot should move forward if there is no obstacle in front of it.
-   If the robot encounters an obstacle, it will check for obstacles to it's left.
    -   If it is clear it will turn left and continue in that direction.
    -   If it is not clear, it will turn left again and check. It will do this a maximum of 4 times. After which it will turn 180 degrees, and try to move forward.

![](assets/pp-preliminary-year-11-paper-bc7f7b57-7ed4-465a-af3d-7e683c60aaae.png)

![](assets/pp-preliminary-year-11-paper-bc7f7b57-7ed4-465a-af3d-7e683c60aaae.png)
prompt:
Write a pseudocode algorithm for the robot vacuum to navigate around a room.

You are to utilise the premade functions and loops into your answer.

criteria.criterion: Substantially correct pseudocode algorithm which meets the scenario
Mostly correct pseudocode algorithm which meets the scenario
Partially correct pseudocode algorithm which meets the scenario
Demonstrates an attempt of an algorithm

sample_answer:
BEGIN ROBOVAC

\# Helper to turn left N times (N \* 30°)
FUNCTION TurnLeftNTimes(N):
    i := 0
    WHILE i < N:
        TurnLeft()
        i := i + 1
END FUNCTION

\# Main loop: run continuously
WHILE TRUE:
    IF NOT CheckObstacle():
        MoveForward()
    ELSE:
        # Obstacle ahead — sweep left up to 4 times (max 120°) to find a clear path
        turns := 0
        path\_found := FALSE

        WHILE turns < 4 AND NOT path\_found:
            TurnLeft()            # rotate 30° left
            turns := turns + 1
            IF NOT CheckObstacle():
                MoveForward()
                path\_found := TRUE

        IF NOT path\_found:
            TurnLeftNTimes(6 - turns)
END WHILE

END ROBOVAC

sample_answer:
Worker safety & duty of care: Carts share the equivalent aisles with people, so a sensor or brake failure could injure workers or damage crops. Ethically, the design needs rich fail safes and procedures to stop the robot.

Security and vendor control (OTA): Requiring weekly updates to run creates dependency and the risk of downtime if an update fails or servers are unreachable. question_title: 19 - OOP - Features of OOP (BHHS, Prelim  Yearly, 2025)
stimulus:
A game design studio is beginning to work on a new 2D action game.

Explain how adopting the object-oriented paradigm (OOP) can streamline the development of the game and reduce maintenance.

In your response, include references to classes, encapsulation, and polymorphism, with examples related to a 2D game.

![](assets/pp-preliminary-year-11-paper-18603792-75c9-47d3-8357-5b74e9d1d48e.png)

![](assets/pp-preliminary-year-11-paper-18603792-75c9-47d3-8357-5b74e9d1d48e.png)

criteria.criterion: Explanation of OOP with reference to classes, encapsulation, and polymorphism, with examples related to a 2D game.
Description of OOP with reference to classes, encapsulation, and polymorphism, with minor reference to a 2D game
Describes OOP with some reference to a 2D game OR classes/encapsulation/polymorphism
Outlines OOP features
Demonstrates some understanding of OOP

sample_answer:
Object-oriented programming (OOP) helps a 2D game feel organised and easier to change. We build classes for the things in the game: a base Entity class with position and sprite, then Player, Enemy, Projectile, and PowerUp that extend it.

Encapsulation means each class keeps its own data safe. For example, Player stores health and collision box privately and offers methods like takeDamage(type) or pickUp(item). Enemies hide their AI state and expose setTarget() instead of random public flags. This stops other code from breaking rules.

Polymorphism lets the game loop treat different objects the same. We can keep a list of Entity and call update(dt) and render() on all of them easily. A Weapon can hit anything that implements IDamageable, so adding a Boss or ShieldedProjectile doesn’t change the loop.

Reusing components like Movement or Health reduces duplicate code, makes teamwork smoother, and keeps bugs contained when we add new features.

**Answers can include:**

Sequential scan: checks each element from start to finish, one by one.

Works everywhere: simple to implement, easy to read, and applies to arrays, Python lists, or any iterable you can loop through.

No sorting required: works on any list/array in any order.
